Thanks Marcus. A couple of quick notes ahead of the workshop so we can land the runbook faster:

- Model variants: If Strata expects mostly short summaries (~128 tokens) we should prioritize a 4-bit quantized variant with dynamic KV cache enabled; reduces cost substantially while keeping latency low. If there are longer context calls (>2048 tokens) we need to test attention scaling and memory footprint.
- Batching approach: suggest a hybrid window (50ms micro-batching) configurable per route. We'll bring benchmark numbers from Redwood Dedicated and Private to compare.
- Security: for Private deployments we assume customer-managed KMS + HSM integration for key wrapping; we will need a list of IP ranges for allowlisting.

I'll draft the perf matrix for the workshop and drop it into the Drive link Marcus provided.

—Camila

- Security: We require SOC 2 evidence plus network allowlist and optional customer-managed KMS. We can provide our compliance questionnaire.

Rachel —

Short answers:

- Presigned URLs: Redwood Private can accept presigned S3 URLs for payload fetch, but best practice is to use a short-lived presign and validate content-size/sha on our side. If you want to offload bandwidth, routing large objects via your CDN is also fine. We'll document allowed header signature patterns in the runbook.
- Concurrency & sizing: For P95 <= 400ms at ~220 concurrency with 128-token responses we recommend a 3-node Dedicated equivalent baseline (A100-like or modern NVLink cluster) with auto-burst headroom. We'll size exactly after running a focused perf sweep.

Proposed tests for the validation run:
1) Smoke: single-request correctness and auth flows (presigned/SIGv4)
2) Perf sweep: ramp to 250 concurrent with typical and worst-case prompt sizes; collect P50/P95/P99
3) Fault injection: simulate a node OOM and validate canary/fallback routes
4) Security test: key rotation and log redaction verification

I'll assemble the test cases and the artifact checklist (coverage matrix + expected logs) and drop a draft in Drive.

Attachments: validation-workshop-agenda.docx
